en.title: Your NID, Phone Number or Personal Data Was Leaked or Misused
en.directAnswer: First identify what information was exposed and what accounts depend on it. Change passwords if login data was involved. Secure email, bank, MFS and social accounts. Check mobile numbers registered under your NID if SIM misuse is possible. Save proof of where the data appeared and any message showing misuse. Bangladesh now has the **Personal Data Protection Act, 2026**, so older guidance based only on the 2025 ordinance should be updated before publication.

atAGlance.mainRule: First identify what information was exposed and what accounts depend on it. Change passwords if login data was involved.

steps: Identify exactly what data was exposed.
Save evidence of the leak or misuse.
Do not publicly repost the full leaked document.
Secure the primary email account first.
Contact bank/MFS provider if financial information was involved.
Check NID-linked SIMs through BTRC NEIR if SIM misuse is possible.
Ask the organisation that held the data for its formal privacy/security contact or complaint process where available.
Consider legal or regulatory complaint routes based on the current Personal Data Protection Act and implementing system.
Report fraud, hacking, threats or blackmail separately where applicable.
evidence: Relevant official notices, receipts, and correspondence
en.simpleExample: A person finds a photo of their NID posted in a public Facebook group. The person should save the post URL and screenshot, ask the platform to remove the image, secure accounts that use NID or phone verification, and monitor for suspicious SIM, banking or account activity. If the NID is then used for fraud, preserve that separate evidence too.
en.specialistTrigger: Large-scale data leak; financial loss; identity theft; employer/customer database breach; sensitive medical/biometric data; repeated misuse; refusal by a data-holding organisation to respond; or a compensation claim.

# Legal Update Register — V1

These update flags should appear in the CMS so a page can be re-reviewed when a law changes.

1. **Registration:** Registration (Amendment) Act, 2026, Act No. 14 of 2026. The current Registration Act shows the section 23 presentation period as three months.
2. **Tax:** Finance Act, 2026 and 2026–27 NBR notices/SROs. All numbers are dynamic.
3. **Labour:** Bangladesh Labour (Amendment) Act, 2026, Act No. 43 of 2026. The 2025 amendment ordinance is not the current amendment instrument.
4. **Cyber:** Cyber Security Act, 2026, Act No. 81 of 2026, plus Cyber Security (Amendment) Act, 2026, Act No. 99 of 2026 dated 1 July 2026. Section 20 is repealed. Pages 41–60 must not use the repealed 2018/2023/2025 cyber statutes as the current primary authority.
5. **Personal data:** Personal Data Protection Act, 2026 is the current primary data-protection statute. Re-check implementing rules, authority procedures and remedies before publishing page 60.
6. **Financial fraud:** Bangladesh Bank CIPC complaint procedure is dynamic. Re-check hotline, email, portal and escalation steps on publication date.
7. **SIM/telecom:** BTRC NEIR currently provides the *16001# NID-linked number check and BTRC maintains an online complaint box. Re-check these operational details before publication.
8. **RTI:** Right to Information (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, dated 9 February 2026.
9. **Legal Aid:** Legal Aid Services (Amendment) Act, 2026, Act No. 45 of 2026.
10. **Family courts:** Family Courts Act, 2023 replaced the Family Courts Ordinance, 1985.
11. **Land:** Land Crime Prevention and Remedy Act, 2023 and Land Reform Act, 2023 are important newer land statutes for selected topics.

# Translation rule

Translate meaning, not legal names. Keep the official English title of an Act in brackets where it helps source verification. Do not make a Bangla translation stronger than the English master. If a legal term has no safe plain-language equivalent, keep the legal term and add a short Bangla explanation.
